rules: Size is the lens's, never enlarged: f/110 mm on the sensor; on a 48 cm-wide sheet 22 px (24 mm lens), 32 px (35 mm), 45 px (50 mm) (layer 1, derived)
Filtered B&W: orange/red filter darkens the blue sky, the brownish-grey Moon keeps its value: Moon 15-30 L* above the sky beside it; suggested sky L* 45-55, highlands L* 70-80 (Ilford; judgement)

FLAG 'brightest': by day the Moon equals sunlit worn asphalt (albedo 0.12; Looney 11 = sunny 16 minus one stop); keep lit skin >= Moon > sky; Moon is the brightest SMALL shape and brightest in the sky, no glint or nail highlight lighter (layer 1, derived)

FLAG 'hardest-edged' with shallow focus: infinity blur f^2/(N(s-f)) is 0.36 mm at f/2.8 (> the 0.22 mm Moon: a dim blot), 0.06 mm at f/16 (crisp, ~1.2 mm rim softening on the sheet); draw it as at f/16 (thin-lens optics, derived)
Lit limb the hardest edge on the disc; terminator a soft half-ellipse (2-4 px at 22 px); unlit part exactly the sky value, no circle outline, no earthshine, no halo by day (layer 1; judgement)
Two or three soft maria 4-8 L* darker than the highlands; no craters at this size (judgement)

Reserve the disc as a hole in the sky's clip region, then tone it up lightly (mech_03 2H/HB, tortillon); soften the rim with one unclipped tortillon pass; no stylus (calibration eraser caps; judgement)
keep: lit limb toward the Sun along the great circle, agreeing with the hand's light
phase shape: semicircular limb, half-ellipse terminator
~0.5 deg of the field of view; oval near a wide frame's corner
avoid: enlarged Moon in a wide-angle picture
paper-white Moon brighter than the sunlit hand
blurred blot (wide aperture) or cut-out hole
outlined full circle, earthshine, glow by day
craters or crisp dark maria at 22 px
lifting the disc out of a dark sky with a too-large eraser
